summary: jenscolt's leg, left and right, as two parametric build123d solids per side: leg-blade (L_leg1) and leg-arm (L_leg2), the right ones (leg-blade-r, leg-arm-r) the same model mirrored about x = 35.45 by a side parameter; the blade's skin from a 5-point spine and 6 control sections (50 numbers), the arm's neck lofted along its own 5-point spine with the hub rigid at its start, so both bend onto N0's leg path by their spines alone (--edit, and leg() for N1); nothing moves.

parts.name: leg-blade
parts.role: the leg's outer blade: a skin lofted along a 5-point spine from 6 control sections with rounded ends, the arm's socket, the side seam grooves and the eye boss carried in the spine's frame
parts.why_separate: a separate jenscolt mesh (L_leg1); N1 form part, not printed

parts.name: leg-arm
parts.role: the leg's arm: hub plate with axle hole, ring and gears (rigid at the spine's start, the crank pin), a ringed neck lofted along a 5-point spine (pin, neck root, pivot, middle, knee) flaring into the top block, the ringed tab tube and the static-leg tab
parts.why_separate: a separate jenscolt mesh (L_leg2); N1 form part, not printed

parts.name: leg-blade-r
parts.role: the right leg's blade: leg-blade mirrored about x = 35.45 (side 'R'), never a second model
parts.why_separate: a separate jenscolt mesh (R_leg1); N1 form part, not printed

parts.name: leg-arm-r
parts.role: the right leg's arm: leg-arm mirrored about x = 35.45 (side 'R'), never a second model
parts.why_separate: a separate jenscolt mesh (R_leg2); N1 form part, not printed

assembly.check: the arm's top block sits in the blade's socket, both in jenscolt's frame
exported in jenscolt's frame, mirror of leg-arm
the right arm's top block sits in the right blade's socket

options: a spine (cubic spline through 5 points) + K control sections, a cubic spline through each number along it
v1's 26 planar sections on a straight axis (≈ 270 numbers)
one section swept along the spine with width / thickness laws (polynomials)
alternatives.choice: a spine (cubic spline through 5 points) + K control sections, a cubic spline through each number along it
alternatives.why: ≤ 60 readable numbers (spine points, widths, thicknesses, roundness) that bend with the spine; v1's table cannot bend and a single swept section loses the tip and the ridge's change along the blade

alternatives.topic: where the features go on a new spine
options: carried in the spine's frame at the same arc-length fraction (n1 warp's convention)
rigid at the same distance from the top end
alternatives.choice: carried in the spine's frame at the same arc-length fraction (n1 warp's convention)
alternatives.why: the sections sit at arc-length fractions too, so socket and eye stay on the skin when the length changes (at a fixed distance the eye floated off the stretched N0 blade)

options: hub rigid at the start of a 5-point spine, neck lofted along it, rings / flare / block / boss placed by z of the original spine mapped knot to knot
v1: 2.5D plate + neck loft on horizontal stations (cannot bend)
one loft along a branched spine
alternatives.choice: hub rigid at the start of a 5-point spine, neck lofted along it, rings / flare / block / boss placed by z of the original spine mapped knot to knot
alternatives.why: N1 lays the arm on N0's inner arm + upper path (crank pin -> pivot -> knee) by its spine alone; mapping knot to knot keeps the pivot on N0's pivot (n1's breakpoints); the hub's flat faces stay exact at 45 degrees

options: side parameter: the left model mirrored about x = 35.45 (or, on given spines, about the leg plane)
a second model with its own numbers
alternatives.choice: side parameter: the left model mirrored about x = 35.45 (or, on given spines, about the leg plane)
alternatives.why: jenscolt's R meshes are the L ones mirrored about x = 35.45 to 0.0000 mm (probe); one model keeps both sides equal under every edit

acceptance.text: four parts, leg-blade (jenscolt L_leg1), leg-arm (L_leg2), leg-blade-r (R_leg1), leg-arm-r (R_leg2), each one valid closed build123d solid, exported by build.py to out/leg-blade.*, out/leg-arm.*, out/leg-blade-r.*, out/leg-arm-r.* (STL and STEP) in jenscolt's own frame at 100 %

the arm's visible details (hub hole, gear relief, the rings, the static-leg tab) present as shape; fine relief may be simplified if fidelity still passes
